metadata.title: Planting Errors to Test a Checker
metadata.audience: Students and practitioners learning to use and report on AI systems
metadata.fellow: Janvi Chitroda, AI Data Engineer volunteer, Medhavy project, Humanitarians AI
metadata.source: inbox/term2-week07/term2-week7-video-content.md (Week 7); narration supplied verbatim and pre-approved by Janvi (2026-10-27)
metadata.note: STEM/learning film, hai Plain register on the ai-explainer chassis. Thesis: when nobody has an answer key, make one — corrupt known-good items on purpose, keep controls, run blind, and measure caught / slipped through / false positives; you only learn about the errors you planted. Worked example: Week 7 sensitivity test. Every on-screen data number appears in the Week 7 source; the Your Turn sizes (ten, five) are Janvi's supplied task.

beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude composer, ask lands answered. Required intro line + AI-narration disclosure.
beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Janvi and this video is about building your own ground truth by planting errors. This narration is an AI-generated voice; the work is mine.

props.command: I want to know how many wrong definitions my checker catches, but I have no answer key. What can I do?
props.segment: Planting Errors to Test a Checker.
output: Corrupt some good items on purpose

beats.role_note: Checker card with 'how many mistakes does it catch?'; empty dashed 'answer key' box; 'so you make it'.
beats.narration_text: To measure how well a checker catches mistakes, you need examples where you already know the answer. Often, nobody has that. So you make it.
beats.visual_intent: Checker card with 'how many mistakes does it catch?'; empty dashed 'answer key' box; 'so you make it'.

show.event: how many mistakes does it catch?

beats.role_note: Flow: good items → corrupted on purpose + kept as controls → checker, blind.
beats.narration_text: Start with items you believe are good. Corrupt some on purpose, keep the rest as controls, and run everything through the checker blind.
beats.visual_intent: Flow: good items → corrupted on purpose + kept as controls → checker, blind.

beats.role_note: Five rows: conflation (BRCA1 as growth promoter, not tumor suppressor) · wrong expansion (ER as endoplasmic reticulum, not estrogen receptor) · disambiguation list · factual error (wrong drug target, wrong organ) · wrong field (industrial / engineering).
beats.narration_text: We used five kinds of corruption: conflation, like describing BRCA1 as a growth promoter instead of a tumor suppressor; a wrong abbreviation expansion; a disambiguation-style list; a specific factual error; and a definition from the wrong field.
beats.visual_intent: Five rows: conflation (BRCA1 as growth promoter, not tumor suppressor) · wrong expansion (ER as endoplasmic reticulum, not estrogen receptor) · disambiguation list · factual error (wrong drug target, wrong organ) · wrong field (industrial / engineering).

beats.role_note: 200 approved → 150 corrupted (30 per type, five boxes of 30) + 50 controls.
beats.narration_text: From 200 approved definitions, we corrupted 150, 30 of each type, and kept 50 as controls.
beats.visual_intent: 200 approved → 150 corrupted (30 per type, five boxes of 30) + 50 controls.

beats.role_note: Three measure cards: caught · slipped through · controls wrongly flagged = false positive rate; our two-judge run in small print (30.0% · 18.7% · 0.0%).
beats.narration_text: Then measure three things: how many corrupted items are caught, how many slip through, and how many good controls get wrongly flagged. That last one is your false positive rate.
beats.visual_intent: Three measure cards: caught · slipped through · controls wrongly flagged = false positive rate; our two-judge run in small print (30.0% · 18.7% · 0.0%).

beats.role_note: Five known types ticked; a sixth dashed chip '?' unticked; captions 'you only learn about the errors you planted' / 'real mistakes can look different'.
beats.narration_text: The limit is that you only learn about the errors you planted. Real mistakes can look different, and a checker can do well on your five types and miss a sixth.
beats.visual_intent: Five known types ticked; a sixth dashed chip '?' unticked; captions 'you only learn about the errors you planted' / 'real mistakes can look different'.

show.event: five types ticked · a sixth missed

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — suggested prompt typed in the composer.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Take ten outputs you trust, break five of them in one specific way, and see how many your checker finds.

props.command: Here are 10 outputs I trust. Break 5 of them in one specific way, mix them in, and don't tell me which.
